author: vladimir_ea
content:
I think the proof end up more or less the same size. I think the advantage is: you can do the recursive aggregation ahead of time (as aggregates arrive), adding total of one slot to the next. And then remove any included in the block. So when you get to your turn you have one additional aggregate to merge which has all attestations not added already.

The removal seems to be generally cheaper than a recursive aggregation.

author: vladimir_ea
content: or do you mean: why not just include all even if on chain already? I think as the number of claims in creases the cost of merging proofs goes up, but actually not sure

author: vladimir_ea
content:
actually it looks like the recursive merge cost is not greatly influenced the number of claims, e.g.:
```
recurse 16 -> 1: 16 proofs, 4929284 bytes, rate 1 -> proof 308376 bytes, 24000 claims, 1.817 s
recurse 16 -> 1: 16 proofs, 2971956 bytes, rate 1 -> proof 284568 bytes, 2400 claims, 1.472 s
```
first case here has 10x more claims. 
so I guess the only advantage of removing is not to include repeats on chain.
